verdict.rationale: Both changes do the same job: they collect every config problem, reject unknown keys, refuse to start and print to stderr with a distinct exit code. A also rejects timeouts too large to convert to milliseconds; otherwise they would later throw ArithmeticException inside ConsoleUplink.send. A leaves the unspecified zero-timeout question to the developer and has more thorough boundary tests. B is slightly better at keeping old behaviour, since it still accepts `TRUE` and `HTTPS` in any case, but it adds a zero-timeout rule the task did not ask for and misses the overflow case.
a_issues: `metrics.enabled` now accepts only lowercase `true`/`false`. The old `Boolean.parseBoolean` accepted `TRUE`/`True`, so existing configs using those will now fail to start.
The URL scheme check is case-sensitive, so `HTTPS://...` is rejected.
A nested `Settings` class sits inside a static utility class. This is a little more structure than needed.
b_issues: It does not reject durations whose millisecond value overflows (e.g. `9223372036854775807s`). These pass validation and then throw ArithmeticException in `ConsoleUplink.send` at runtime.
It adds a new rule rejecting a zero timeout and changes the README wording. The task did not ask for this, though the report does flag it.
A missing file gets only the generic 'Cannot read configuration file ... NoSuchFileException' message, not a clear 'not found'.
Tests are less thorough: no int-overflow case, no present-but-empty value, no blank token, and no full set of minimum-boundary acceptance checks.

verdict.rationale: Both changes turn every silent fallback into a collected ConfigException, reject unknown keys, keep defaults for absent keys and exit with a distinct code. B also rejects timeouts too large for the uplink's `toMillis()` call, which A lets through to crash later at send time. B keeps the existing rule that a zero timeout is allowed and flags the question, and its tests cover more boundaries. B's case-sensitive `true`/`false` and http/https scheme checks are a small regression against the old lenient parsing that A preserves.
a_issues: Rejects `request.timeout=0s`, a behavior change the original rules did not call for (though it is reported and documented).
Does not reject timeouts that overflow `toMillis()`, e.g. `9223372036854775807s`, so `ConsoleUplink` would throw at runtime instead of at startup.
Fewer boundary tests: no test that the minimum values are accepted for all numeric keys, and no int-overflow or empty-value tests.
b_issues: `metrics.enabled` now requires exact lowercase `true`/`false`; the old `Boolean.parseBoolean` accepted `TRUE`, so existing configs could stop starting.
The URL scheme check is case-sensitive, so `HTTPS://...` is rejected.
No test protects the claim that the API token is never echoed.
